jobs.title: Chief Product Officer
jobs.description:
Position Overview

The Chief Product Officer builds and leads Jaza’s product function and owns product strategy across two verticals: Consumer, which is what our customers get (packs, charging, hubs, energy systems, pricing, and the customer app), and Enterprise, the tools Jaza runs on (Star App, Site App, our Dashboard and data platform, and our payments infrastructure).

Jaza has been engineering-led. Product decisions have been made by the people building the product. We are now creating Product as its own function, so that what we build is driven by customer outcomes and unit economics. We define our product by the customer’s energy outcome, not by the delivery mechanism. Battery swap is how we deliver that outcome today. You will hold that line, decide with evidence when the product should change, and own Jaza Lab, where we test new products and new ways of delivering energy before we commit capital to them.

Success in your first year: a product strategy and a single roadmap across both verticals tied to the company plan and unit economics; product practice running in both verticals; the product team built around the two Product Leads; and Jaza Lab running as a portfolio with a ring-fenced budget and clear stage gates.

Roles And Responsibilities

The Chief Product Officer responsibilities include, but are not limited to, the following:

Product strategy and outcomes (35%)

Own Jaza’s product strategy and the cross-vertical roadmap.
Own product outcomes. For Consumer: active customers, revenue per customer, cost per kWh delivered, and capital cost per customer. For Enterprise: operating cost per customer, uptime, and data coverage.
Run the gates on capital-heavy decisions (pack and hub specifications, pricing, and major releases) with engineering and finance, including a financial and technical risk check before capital is committed. A hardware specification commits capital across thousands of sites; a software release can stop revenue in the field.
Make safety, regulatory, and certification requirements a criterion at every stage gate, working with Quality, HSE, and Legal.

Product leadership and team building (30% )

Lead and develop the Product Leads for Consumer and Enterprise and the Jaza Lab Lead, and build the product organization beneath them.
Get product practice running in both verticals: discovery, product requirements, stage gates sized to capital at risk, and post-launch reviews that change decisions.

Jaza Lab (15%)

Own Jaza Lab, our R&D and pilot engine for new products and new delivery mechanisms: take ideas from concept to proof of concept to pilot, set its budget with the CEO and CFO, and kill what does not work quickly and cheaply.

Customer voice, board, and leadership (20%)

Own customer voice and employee voice across the company.
Partner with the CTO, who owns delivery across hardware, software, and data.
Represent product to the board, investors, the leadership team, and key partners.

Key Performance Indicators (KPIs)

Active customers, retention, and revenue per customer (Consumer).
Cost per kWh delivered and capital cost per customer (Consumer).
Operating cost per customer, uptime, data coverage, and capacity utilization across sites (Enterprise).
Jaza Lab portfolio: ideas stopped or scaled at each stage gate against budget.

Key Working Relationships

Chief Executive Officer (reporting line).
Chief Technology Officer (delivery across hardware, software, and data).
Product Lead, Consumer; Product Lead, Enterprise; and Jaza Lab Lead.
Chief Financial Officer.
Country leadership and operations teams across our markets.
The board.

Why You Should Apply

Be part of the most exciting growth phase of a company. We’ve proven our model and are focused on expansion. This position entails high impact, visibility, and opportunities to advance quickly.
Work with great teammates in an international environment. Our team is spread across Canada, China, Tanzania, Nigeria, and Kenya. You’ll be interfacing with our CEO, CTO, and leadership team on a regular basis.
Gain hands-on business building experience. Although we are a startup, we don’t expect you to just figure it out on your own. You’ll be given lots of responsibility but also lots of support to help you succeed.

Qualifications

Industry Knowledge: A product P&L you have owned at scale in emerging markets, for example in energy, mobile money, telco, or consumer fintech.
Management and Leadership Skills: At least 5 years leading product organizations that span hardware and software, or physical and digital offers. Experience building a function from an early stage, including hiring and developing senior leaders.
Professional Experience: 10+ years of executive product leadership in technology, hardware and software, or clean-tech environments.
Technical Skills: The ability to set strategy and also run detailed gate reviews on capital-heavy decisions.
Interpersonal Skills: Credibility with a board and leadership team on unit economics. Willingness to spend substantial time in our markets, and a genuine commitment to Jaza’s mission of solving global energy access.
Language Proficiency: Fluent written and spoken English.

Must have skills

Emerging Market P&L Ownership
Executive Leadership Experience
Hardware & Software Product Leadership
Emerging Market Scale

jobs.description:
About Powerfleet

Powerfleet (Nasdaq: AIOT; JSE: PWR) is a global leader in the artificial intelligence of things (AIoT) software-as-a-service (SaaS) mobile asset industry. With more than 30 years of experience, Powerfleet unifies business operations through the ingestion, harmonization, and integration of data—regardless of source—and delivers actionable insights to help companies meet their strategic objectives around Safety, Compliance, Efficiency and Sustainability. Our people-first culture and relentless innovation empower customers to achieve measurable, sustainable business improvements. Powerfleet serves over 2.6 million subscribers across more than 48,000 customers in 120 countries, with commercial operations across every major continent.

Position Overview

The Collections Director leads the North American collections function and is accountable for cash delivery, forecasting, collectability analysis and resolution of complex customer balances. This is not a traditional collections role. The position requires significant research and cross-functional problem solving, including locating historical contracts, resolving billing and credit issues, and obtaining evidence that sold devices are active on the data platform.

Key Responsibilities

Lead, coach and develop a team consisting of one Collections Manager and six Collections Analysts, with clear account ownership, priorities and escalation paths.
Responsible for enforcing corporate processes
Consolidate disjointed collections teams and processes across North America into a consistent operating model with standardized reporting, documentation and customer treatment.
Lead the implementation and adoption of the Advanced Collections module in Microsoft Dynamics 365, including workflows, work queues, account segmentation, notes, promise-to-pay tracking and management reporting.
Oversee negotiations and resolution strategies for large and complex customers, including accounts affected by incorrect billing, disputed charges, legacy arrangements and credits to be issued.
Partner with Billing and other teams to prioritize research and corrective actions based on value, aging, customer impact, collectability risk and expected cash recovery.
Coordinate research of historical contracts, amendments, billing records and operational data needed to substantiate amounts due and resolve customer disputes.
Work with operational and data-platform stakeholders to obtain evidence that devices sold to customers are active, deployed or otherwise supported by system data.
Own the North American collections forecast, including expected timing, risks, assumptions and major account dependencies.
Maintain the cash target file and ensure timely, accurate input by the collections team, with clear tracking of actual results against forecast and target.
Prepare and present monthly executive reporting on specific customer accounts, including collectability, unresolved issues, expected cash timing, credits, dependencies and recommended next steps.
Identify recurring causes of delayed payment and partner with upstream teams to reduce preventable billing, contracting, data and process issues.

Qualifications And Experience

10+ years of experience in collections with Enterprise Fortune 1000 company.
Progressive experience in collections, accounts receivable, order-to-cash, credit or finance operations, including leadership of multi-level teams.
Demonstrated success resolving large, complex or disputed customer balances through research, negotiation and cross-functional coordination.
Strong experience in collections forecasting, customer collectability analysis and executive-level reporting.
Experience leading process consolidation or finance transformation across multiple teams, business units or geographies.
Experience with Microsoft Dynamics 365 collections capabilities or a comparable enterprise platform; Advanced Collections implementation experience is preferred.
Strong analytical and commercial judgment, with the ability to connect contracts, billing records, credits, customer history and operational data into clear conclusions.
Advanced Excel skills and experience using reporting or business intelligence tools.
Bachelor’s degree in Finance, Accounting, Business or a related discipline, or equivalent relevant experience.

Measures of Success

Achievement of cash targets and improved forecasting accuracy.
Reduction in aged and unresolved balances, particularly for high-value and complex accounts.
Timely resolution of billing errors, credits, disputes and supporting-evidence requirements.
Effective adoption of Dynamics 365 Advanced Collections and consistent North American processes.
Clear, decision-ready executive reporting on customer collectability and collection risk.

A gateway for transportation, connection, and innovation, Edmonton Airports (YEG) is a self-funded, not-for-profit corporation driving economic prosperity for the Edmonton Metropolitan Region and beyond. Edmonton Airports employs 250-300 employees, offering challenging, rewarding opportunities that allows team members to thrive in what they do. The work culture is known for being open, collaborative, and inclusive. Recognizing that great work gets accomplished when people enjoy what they’re doing, successes and milestones are always celebrated. As strong believers in the power of setting professional goals and continuously encouraging team members to do so on a regular basis, YEG appreciates feedback on how it can support and enhance partnerships that exist on the corporate team. YEG values opportunities to create diversity within teams, including backgrounds, experiences, perspectives, and ways of working together. Seeking positive, enthusiastic people who are not afraid to take on challenges, YEG aims to create a community of unique individuals to allow for expanded ideas, perspectives, and better business decisions. A core value of YEG is "investing in our talent" and it considers professional development, specialty training, and career growth among its top priorities to expand team member skillset and continue evolving as new technology and ideas evolve.

In addition to propelling a positive work culture internally, the airport land is home to over 250 businesses looking to expand tourism, entertainment, cargo logistics, manufacturing, sustainability, innovative technology development, and commercialization. 4-Day Work Week | Leadership Role | Winnipeg, Manitoba

McLenehan and Associates Chartered Professional Accountants
$140,000 Base Salary | 32-Hour Week, Even in Busy Season | Lead the Department, Shape the Firm

WHY YOU'LL LOVE WORKING HERE

4-Day Work Week
Four 8-hour days. In public practice. Through busy season. Yes, really.
Competitive Salary
$140,000 base. Full-time pay for a 32-hour week.
Real Authority
You run the public practice department: the people, the production, the processes, and the quality standard. You report to the owner, and no one else.
Generous Time Off
3 weeks of vacation plus a paid week during the December holidays.
Paid Growth
Firm-funded professional development and your annual CPD, covered.
RRSP Matching
Contribution matching to support your long-term financial security.
Comprehensive Benefits
Prescription, dental, and vision coverage.

THE OPPORTUNITY

Most senior roles in public practice follow the same script. You carry the team, but someone else makes the decisions. You review files until nine at night in March. You are told the firm values balance, and then busy season arrives and the promise quietly expires.

This one is different.

McLenehan and Associates CPAs is a growing Winnipeg-based accounting firm serving hundreds of incorporated Canadian small businesses, from monthly bookkeeping and year-end compliance through to Fractional CFO and Virtual Controller services. Our people like the work they do and the people they do it with. And our 4-day work week has proven, for years, that high standards and a full life outside the office are not in conflict.
Until now, the final review of year-end files, the delivery of finished work to clients, and the day-to-day leadership of our public practice team have run through Mike McLenehan, the firm's owner. As the firm has grown, that has made Mike the bottleneck, and it has kept him from the work only an owner can do: strategy, growth, and building the firm. That changes with this hire.

We are putting Directors in place who hold full responsibility for their departments. A Director of Business Development and a Director of People and Culture are already in their seats. The Director of Public Practice is an important addition to that leadership team, taking ownership of the department at the centre of the firm: year-end preparation, corporate tax, and personal tax.

This is the senior seat that experienced CPAs talk about but rarely find: a firm with 500 to 600 incorporated business owner clients, a department of Managers, Assistant Managers, Senior Accountants, and Accountants ready to report to you, a proven 4-day work week, and an owner who is ready to hand you the department and support your decisions.

To be clear, this is not a role that takes you out of the work. You will review files, you will sit across from business owners and deliver their results, and you will hold ultimate responsibility for the quality of everything that leaves the department. What is different is that you will also own the system that produces that work: the workflow, the capacity planning, the processes, and the people.

We are not looking for someone to grow into this role. We are looking for someone who has already done this work: reviewed the files, led the people, sat with the owners, and run a busy season. Someone who wants to do it inside a firm that respects their time and their judgment.

If that describes you, keep reading.

WHAT YOU'LL EARN

Base Salary:
$140,000

Work Week:
Four 8-hour days. 32 hours. Year-round, including personal tax season and corporate year-end peaks

Time Off:
3 weeks of vacation plus a paid week during the December holidays

Retirement:
RRSP contribution matching

Health Benefits:
Prescription, dental, and vision coverage

Professional Development:
Annual CPD covered, plus firm-funded development in leadership and advisory skills

Reporting Line:
Directly to Mike McLenehan, the firm's owner. No layers in between

Location:
In-office, Winnipeg. This is a senior leadership role and the team is here

Public practice has trained most senior CPAs to quietly accept that a strong salary comes bundled with a brutal spring. Here, the salary is full-time and the week is 32 hours. Work out what that does to your effective hourly rate compared with your last busy season, and then keep reading.

THE DEPARTMENT YOU'LL LEAD

The clients

500 to 600 incorporated, owner-managed Canadian small businesses: trades, professionals, retailers, contractors, and holding companies. They are building something meaningful, they want advice they can act on, and they want to hear it from someone who speaks their language.

The work

Year-end compilation and review engagements, corporate tax returns (T2), personal tax returns (T1), and owner-manager tax planning: compensation planning, corporate structures, and the purchase and sale of a business. We do not perform audit engagements. The department exists to deliver compliance work of a consistently high standard and to turn that work into advice our clients value.

The team

The department is made up of Managers, Assistant Managers, Senior Accountants, and Accountants. You lead all of them. Your Managers share responsibility with you for quality assurance and quality review on every file, and you hold ultimate responsibility for what leaves the department. Mike's partner sign-off remains on client deliverables.

Your tools

CCH iFirm for practice management and iFirm Tax for every T1 and T2. CaseWare with Jazzit financial statement templates for year-end preparation. QuickBooks Online across most client files. You will have a strong voice in what we adopt next.

How we will work together

Strategy, hiring, compensation, processes, budgets, and software are decided together, you and Mike. Implementation is yours, and so is the result. Mike will be alongside you for the first several weeks of file reviews and client meetings until you are calibrated to the firm's standard, and then his involvement shifts to partner sign-off, the most complex matters, and the strategic decisions you bring to him.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

Lead the Public Practice Department

Own the production system for year-end preparation, corporate tax, and personal tax: workflow, capacity planning, scheduling, and deadlines across the full year, including T1 season and corporate year-end peaks
Design, document, and continuously improve the department's processes so that quality and turnaround do not depend on any one person, including you
Set and monitor the department's KPIs, including turnaround time, budget versus actual on files, deadlines met, and review points, and report on them regularly to Mike
Lead the department's software and workflow improvements in iFirm, CaseWare, and the tools around them, in coordination with the firm's leadership team

Quality Assurance and File Review

Hold ultimate responsibility for quality assurance and quality review across the department, working with your Managers, who share the review workload with you
Review year-end compilation and review engagement files, corporate tax returns (T2), and personal tax returns (T1) before they reach the partner for sign-off, with a focus on the complex, the unusual, and the high-stakes
Uphold the firm's quality standards and professional requirements on every file, and know when an issue needs to be escalated
Coach preparers and reviewers through your review notes so the same issues stop recurring. Your goal is fewer review points every season, not more

Client Delivery and Advisory

Meet with business owner clients to deliver finished year-end results and tax returns, and explain them in plain language the owner can act on
Provide financial and tax advice on owner-manager matters: compensation planning (salary versus dividends), corporate structures, purchase and sale of a business, and CRA correspondence
Identify opportunities where clients would benefit from deeper advisory services, and coordinate with our Director of Business Development to grow those relationships

People Leadership

Lead and develop the department's Managers, Assistant Managers, Senior Accountants, and Accountants across the full people cycle: hiring input, onboarding, training, coaching, performance evaluations, and career development
Build the bench: develop Senior Accountants into reviewers and Assistant Managers into Managers, and make the department stronger every quarter
Work with our Director of People and Culture on recruiting, performance management, and career pathways for the department

WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE: YOUR FIRST 90 DAYS

Month 1 (Days 1 to 30): Learning the firm

You know our clients, services, systems, and standards well enough to hold a credible advisory conversation
You have met one-on-one with every member of the department and understand their strengths, goals, and development needs
You are shadowing file reviews and client meetings alongside Mike and calibrating to the firm's quality bar
You have mapped the department's current workflow from client request to partner sign-off and identified where it slows down

Month 2 (Days 31 to 60): Taking the Reins

You and your Managers are completing file reviews independently on standard files, with Mike involved only on complex matters
Workload planning, scheduling, and day-to-day leadership of the department run through you
You are joining client meetings and beginning to lead them
You have agreed a set of department KPIs with Mike and begun reporting on them

Month 3 (Days 61 to 90): Fully Operational

The department's production and quality review run through you and your Managers, and Mike's role has narrowed to partner sign-off and the most complex files
You own the team: performance management, development plans, and hiring input are yours

WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

7+ years of Canadian public practice experience, including several years reviewing files prepared by others
Deep, current expertise in compilation and review engagements, corporate tax (T2), personal tax (T1), and owner-manager tax planning
Proven experience leading a team of accounting professionals in public practice, including managing Managers or Senior Accountants who review the work of others
The presence and judgment to sit across from a business owner, hold the conversation, and give advice they trust
A track record of running a busy season: planning capacity, managing a team's workload, and meeting competing deadlines without dropping the standard

You will stand out if you have:

Experience as the final reviewer in a firm, or as a Senior Manager or Principal with responsibility for a department's production and quality
Hands-on experience with CaseWare and Jazzit, CCH iFirm and iFirm Tax, and QuickBooks Online, or comparable tools
Experience designing or implementing workflow and process improvements in a growing firm, and measuring the results
Exposure to advisory work beyond compliance: cash flow, budgeting, business purchase and sale, or CFO-level conversations

WHO YOU ARE

Top performers will recognize themselves in this list:

You have the technical judgment to be the last word on a file, and the self-awareness to know when to pick up the phone and talk it through
You think in systems. When a file goes sideways, you fix the file and then you fix the process that let it happen
You find genuine satisfaction in a clean file, and equal satisfaction in coaching the person who prepared it
Your review notes teach; they do not just correct
Business owners relax when you walk into the room, because you speak their language, not just the Income Tax Act's

At Gore Mutual, we’ve always set ourselves apart as a modern mutual that does good. Now, we’re proudly building on that legacy to transform our company—and our industry—for the better.
Effective January 1, 2026, Gore has joined Beneva—the country’s largest mutual insurance company—as part of its Property & Casualty operations in Ontario and Western Canada. During 2026, Gore will combine its operations with Unica Insurance, Beneva’s Ontario-based subsidiary specializing in niche commercial and personal insurance, creating a stronger, more diversified mutual insurer with greater scale and long-term stability.
Every decision and investment remains anchored in long-term benefits to customers, members, and communities. Come join us.
We are looking for a Director, Data Engineering to lead a critical capability within Gore’s Enterprise Data & Analytics organization. You will lead the teams responsible for turning enterprise data into trusted, reusable data products and building the engineering capabilities that enable Data, Insights and AI across Gore.
You will shape how we build and manage data products, evolve our Data Engineering and MLOps capabilities, and ensure our Databricks and Azure ecosystem provides the foundation needed for Analytics, Data Science, GenAI and emerging AI solutions.
This is a visible leadership role for someone who combines strong technical depth with business understanding, people leadership and the ability to turn data and technology investments into meaningful business outcomes.
What will you do?

Build Enterprise Data Products

Lead the development of trusted, reusable data products that combine business meaning, data quality and strong engineering to support operational, analytical, Data Science and AI use cases.
Establish and mature our data product discipline, partnering with business and technology leaders to turn high-value data needs into scalable capabilities.
Improve the accessibility, consistency and value of enterprise data while reducing fragmentation and duplication.

Advance Data Engineering & AI Enablement

Lead and mature Data Engineering and MLOps capabilities, creating repeatable paths to move data, machine learning, GenAI and emerging AI solutions into secure, reliable production.
Raise engineering standards across integration, APIs, orchestration, CI/CD, testing, observability, automation, data quality and production operations.
Partner across Data, Analytics and technology teams to provide the engineering capabilities needed to scale Data Science and AI.

Evolve Our Data Technology Foundation

Guide the evolution of Gore’s Databricks and Azure ecosystem to provide a scalable, resilient, secure and cost-effective foundation for Data, Insights and AI.
Partner with IT and Architecture to shape architecture patterns, integration approaches and technology standards.
Evaluate emerging Data and AI technologies based on business value, scalability, security and long-term sustainability.

Build and Lead a Strong Engineering Organization

Lead, coach and develop high-performing teams across Data Products, Data Platforms, Data Engineering and MLOps.
Develop strong managers and technical leaders with clear accountability for products, engineering quality and production outcomes.
Build a culture of ownership, curiosity, continuous improvement and engineering excellence.

Provide Visible Enterprise Leadership

Represent Data Engineering with senior business and technology leaders, vendors and strategic partners.
Translate complex technology decisions into clear business implications, trade-offs, risks and recommendations.
Provide clear leadership across priorities, investments, delivery and significant operational challenges.

What will you need to succeed?

A degree in Computer Science, Engineering, Data or a related discipline, or equivalent relevant experience
Significant leadership experience across Data Engineering, data products, data platforms, MLOps or related enterprise technology functions.
Proven experience building enterprise data products and translating business needs into reusable, scalable data capabilities.
Proven experience building and operating enterprise-scale data platforms and production data workloads.
Direct production experience with Databricks, including data engineering, lakehouse architecture, governance and optimization.
Strong experience with Microsoft Azure and modern cloud data architectures.
Strong technical knowledge of Python, SQL, APIs, data integration, orchestration and distributed processing.
Experience with technologies such as Delta Lake, Unity Catalog and MLflow, or comparable capabilities.
Experience with CI/CD, automated testing, observability, DevOps, DataOps and modern production engineering practices.
Practical MLOps experience enabling Data Science, machine learning and AI workloads in production.
Experience enabling GenAI or emerging AI capabilities in secure enterprise environments.
A strong track record of coaching and developing engineers, managers and technical leaders.
Strong executive presence and the ability to influence senior business, technology and external stakeholders.

At Husky TechnologiesTM, our success is based on your success. Our ability to keep our customers in the lead is based on building the strongest team possible.

Husky TechnologiesTM has a strong foundation built on innovation, close customer relationships and a unique culture and values. We are dedicated to offering our customers the highest quality products and services and are looking for people with the inspiration and talent to develop with us as we pursue our ambitious growth strategy. We are a leader in developing state-of-the-art technology and it is this technology base that uniquely positions us to serve customers who seek differentiation through solutions that provide speed, flexibility and maximum productivity. This capability is at the core of our mission and competitive strategy.

Husky TechnologiesTM offers a wealth of opportunity for personal growth and development. Most importantly, Husky Technologies TM offers an opportunity to work with – and be challenged by – a team of great people. Our success is possible because of the creativity, intelligence and passion of our people around the world and their desire to lead change. At the same time, we are not afraid to expect a lot and strive for leadership in all of our key markets. We are a company taking on new challenges and for the right people this means exceptional career development opportunities, the chance to be part of a team that is the best in the world at what we do and the experience that comes from working in an environment that demands constant transformation and innovation.

Husky TechnologiesTM is an exciting company with tremendous potential. We have a great team and great expectations. If you are attracted to bold goals, believe in uncompromising honesty, support mutual respect, care about environmental responsibility, have a passion for excellence and a desire to make a positive contribution – then we want you to join the Husky TechnologiesTM team!

The Finance Director serves as a strategic business partner to the Leadership Team in support of Husky’s Global Service Business and Customer Success Management strategy. This role provides leadership for financial planning, forecasting, performance analysis, governance, and decision support to drive profitable growth, improve operational performance, and strengthen financial visibility across service revenue streams, including field service, contracts, parts, and other aftermarket offerings. The Finance Director is expected to influence strategic decisions, lead transformation initiatives, and build a high-performing finance capability that enables the business to scale effectively.

Key Responsibilities

Financial Planning & Forecasting

Lead the annual budget, quarterly forecast, and long-range planning processes for the service business.
Develop robust revenue, margin, cost, and headcount forecasts based on operational and commercial drivers.
Translate business strategies into financial plans with clear assumptions, risks, and opportunities.
Support scenario planning and sensitivity analysis for service growth, pricing, labor utilization, and investment decisions.

Performance Management & Analysis

Deliver timely and accurate monthly financial reporting and variance analysis for service revenue, gross margin, SG&A, and operating income.
Analyze business performance by region, product line, customer segment, channel, and service offering.
Monitor and explain key drivers of performance, including labor utilization, absorption, contract profitability, attach rates, response times, and service productivity.
Provide actionable insights and recommendations to improve growth, profitability, and working capital performance.

Business Partnering

Serve as the senior finance partner to service leadership, operations, commercial teams, and Customer Success leaders, providing insight and challenge on strategic priorities, business performance, and investment decisions.
Lead financial evaluation of pricing strategies, contract renewals, service program design, and capital or operating investments to support sustainable growth and margin expansion.
Provide proactive challenge and decision support to business leaders by identifying risks, opportunities, and trade-offs across growth, productivity, service delivery, and resource allocation.
Lead cross-functional evaluation of new service offerings, business models, and transformation initiatives that improve service coverage, utilization, fulfillment, cost efficiency, and customer value.
Sponsor finance and business transformation initiatives across Finance and Customer Success Management, including enhancements to processes, reporting, operating metrics, and decision frameworks that support growth, profitability, and scalability.

Management Reporting & KPI Development

Develop and enhance dashboards, reporting tools, and KPIs that improve transparency and decision-making.
Standardize definitions and reporting for critical service metrics across the organization.
Improve reporting automation and self-service analytics capabilities where possible.
Present clear financial results and business insights to senior leadership

Process Improvement & Governance

Strengthen forecasting accuracy, reporting discipline, and financial controls within the service business.
Drive continuous improvement in FP&A processes, planning models, and reporting frameworks.
Ensure alignment with corporate finance requirements, accounting policies, and internal controls
Support month-end close and planning processes in partnership with accounting and finance teams.

Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in Finance, Accounting, Economics, or a related field required.
CPA, CMA, CFA, or MBA preferred.
10+ years of progressive experience in FP&A, finance business partnering, commercial finance, or operational finance, including leadership responsibility.
Experience in a service, aftermarket, field service, maintenance, or contract-based business strongly preferred.
Strong financial modeling, forecasting, and business analysis skills.
Advanced proficiency in Excel and experience with ERP and planning/reporting systems.
Executive presence with strong communication, presentation, and stakeholder management skills, and the ability to influence senior leaders across functions and regions.
Proven ability to work cross-functionally in a fast-paced, performance-driven environment

Preferred Experience In a Service Business

Understanding of service revenue models such as time and materials, service contracts, preventive maintenance, subscriptions, and parts/service bundles.
Experience analyzing operational KPIs such as technician utilization, service efficiency, contract margins, backlog, renewal rates, and service attach rates.
Familiarity with pricing strategy, labor productivity, installed base analytics, and customer lifecycle economics

Core Competencies

Strategic leadership
Financial and commercial acumen
Analytical rigor
Executive business partnership
Influence and executive communication
Problem solving
Process improvement
Results orientation and a bias for action

Mettre en œuvre des processus pour garantir que des informations complètes, fiables et robustes sont utilisées pour la prise de décision.
Interpréter, déchiffrer et synthétiser plusieurs sources de données en utilisant SQL.
Diriger la mise en œuvre des meilleures pratiques analytiques dans les départements de recrutement, médical et de performance.

Perform other related tasks and responsibilities.

Passion pour l'amélioration des processus, le sport, l'analyse de données et le soccer.
Un minimum de cinq (5) ans d'expérience dans un rôle d'analyse et d'interprétation de données, de préférence dans l'industrie du sport et du soccer.

Des études supérieures tel qu’une maitrise ou un doctorat dans un domaine connexe, sont un atout.

Financial Planning & Forecasting

Lead the annual budget, quarterly forecast, and long-range planning processes for the service business.
Develop robust revenue, margin, cost, and headcount forecasts based on operational and commercial drivers.
Translate business strategies into financial plans with clear assumptions, risks, and opportunities.
Support scenario planning and sensitivity analysis for service growth, pricing, labor utilization, and investment decisions.

Improve reporting automation and self-service analytics capabilities where possible.
Present clear financial results and business insights to senior leadership

Drive continuous improvement in FP&A processes, planning models, and reporting frameworks.
Ensure alignment with corporate finance requirements, accounting policies, and internal controls
Support month-end close and planning processes in partnership with accounting and finance teams.

CPA, CMA, CFA, or MBA preferred.
10+ years of progressive experience in FP&A, finance business partnering, commercial finance, or operational finance, including leadership responsibility.
Experience in a service, aftermarket, field service, maintenance, or contract-based business strongly preferred.
Strong financial modeling, forecasting, and business analysis skills.
Advanced proficiency in Excel and experience with ERP and planning/reporting systems.
Executive presence with strong communication, presentation, and stakeholder management skills, and the ability to influence senior leaders across functions and regions.
Proven ability to work cross-functionally in a fast-paced, performance-driven environment

Understanding of service revenue models such as time and materials, service contracts, preventive maintenance, subscriptions, and parts/service bundles.
Experience analyzing operational KPIs such as technician utilization, service efficiency, contract margins, backlog, renewal rates, and service attach rates.
Familiarity with pricing strategy, labor productivity, installed base analytics, and customer lifecycle economics

Strategic leadership
Financial and commercial acumen

Problem solving

Results orientation and a bias for action

Build and lead a high-performing finance team with strong capability in financial analysis, strategic thinking, business partnership, and change leadership.
